job.style: a passage rich in numbers, dates or measurements

passage: The Earth is a complex system composed of four major domains that interact to sustain life. The lithosphere is the solid portion of the Earth, while the atmosphere is the gaseous layer that surrounds our planet. The atmosphere is composed of 78 percent nitrogen, 21 percent oxygen, and 1 percent other gases like argon and carbon dioxide. The hydrosphere covers 71 percent of the Earth's surface, primarily as oceans. These vast water bodies are not uniform; the salinity of ocean water varies significantly depending on evaporation and freshwater inflow from rivers. The continents are massive landmasses that are part of the Earth's crust, resting on tectonic plates rather than floating on water. Finally, the biosphere is the narrow zone where land, water, and air interact to support life. This zone is not limited to the surface of the land; it extends deep into the oceans and high into the atmosphere, creating a vast space where living organisms thrive. Whether it is deep-sea creatures in the dark trenches or birds flying at high altitudes, life exists far beyond just the ground we walk on.

items.evidence: The atmosphere is composed of 78 percent nitrogen, 21 percent oxygen, and 1 percent other gases like argon and carbon dioxide.
items.q: If you split air into 100 equal parts, which gas would fill the most parts?
items.explain: Air is 78 percent nitrogen and only 21 percent oxygen, so nitrogen fills most parts.

wrong.why: thinks oxygen is the most common gas in air
mixes up the gases with their numbers
picks the 71 percent figure from the hydrosphere sentence

items.evidence: These vast water bodies are not uniform; the salinity of ocean water varies significantly depending on evaporation and freshwater inflow from rivers.
items.q: Sea A gets much river water. Sea B loses much water to evaporation. Which is likely saltier?
options: Sea B, as water leaves but salt stays
Sea A, as rivers pour salt into it
Sea A, as more water holds more salt
Neither, all ocean water is equally salty
items.explain: Saltiness depends on evaporation and river inflow. Evaporation takes away water but leaves the salt behind.

wrong.why: gets the effect of fresh river water backwards
thinks more water means more salt
thinks all ocean water is equally salty

items.evidence: The continents are massive landmasses that are part of the Earth's crust, resting on tectonic plates rather than floating on water.
items.q: What do the continents rest on?
options: Tectonic plates, not a layer of water
Ocean water, like giant floating islands
The hydrosphere that covers most of Earth
The biosphere zone where all life thrives
items.explain: Continents are part of the Earth's crust and rest on tectonic plates. They do not float on water.

wrong.why: thinks continents float on the ocean like islands
picks the water domain mentioned just before
picks a nearby domain named in the passage

items.evidence: This zone is not limited to the surface of the land; it extends deep into the oceans and high into the atmosphere, creating a vast space where living organisms thrive.
items.q: A fish lives in a dark trench deep in the ocean. Is it part of the biosphere?
options: Yes, the biosphere reaches deep into the oceans
No, the biosphere covers only the land surface
No, the hydrosphere is separate from the biosphere
Yes, but only if it swims near the surface
items.explain: The biosphere is not only on land. It reaches deep into the oceans, where deep-sea creatures live.

wrong.why: thinks the biosphere is only on land
thinks the domains are separate and do not overlap
thinks the life zone is only shallow water
